free_tier.stated: A USD 1.00 welcome credit on every new account, and one on-demand GPU model: RTX Pro 6000 (96 GB) at USD 1.89 per GPU-hour, billed per second with no minimum commitment. The GPU page says eligible accounts can try a single GPU with less than one hour of credit, subject to a minimum launch balance, capacity and account limits. None of H100, A100 80 GB, L40S, RTX 4090 or L4 is listed. Eight-GPU nodes show 'On request'; reserved nodes are by contract.

per_object_cap.notes: the sizes are 1, 2, 4 or 8 RTX Pro 6000 GPUs on one host

retention.stated: Terminating the instance releases its GPU and deletes temporary container data. Cloud drives and shared filesystems remain and continue billing until deleted.
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the container's temporary data

egress.terms: not stated on the pricing or GPU pages read

interface_detail: stated by a third-party listing, not probed: containerized Linux instances with SSH, a browser terminal and Jupyter; an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API at api.ecohash.com for models
tooling: launch from the console at console.ecohash.com: a compute template and a 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPU size, then SSH, the browser terminal or Jupyter. Models are called through an OpenAI-compatible API with an API key.
chaining: the USD 1.00 credit buys less than an hour of the one GPU model; the offer is a trial of RTX Pro 6000 time and a paid rental after it.

limits.value: USD 1.00 one-time welcome credit; the GPU page states a minimum launch balance and account limits without giving the amounts
